full_query: A 27-year-old man presents for an appointment to establish care. He recently was released from prison. He has felt very fatigued and has had a cough. He has lost roughly 15 pounds over the past 3 weeks. He attributes this to intravenous drug use in prison. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. QuantiFERON gold testing is positive. The patient is started on appropriate treatment. Which of the following is the most likely indication to discontinue this patient's treatment? (A) Elevated liver enzymes (B) Hyperuricemia (C) Optic neuritis (D) Peripheral neuropathy (E) Red body excretions

sentences: To determine the most appropriate answer to the question, we'll analyze each option step-by-step
Step 1: Understanding the Clinical Scenario
The patient has been diagnosed with tuberculosis (TB) based on a positive QuantiFERON gold test
He is being started on appropriate treatment for TB
Step 2: Recognizing Common Anti-Tuberculosis Medications and Side Effects
The standard initial treatment for active TB typically includes a combination of isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol
We will consider the side effects of these medications to determine which one would warrant discontinuation of treatment
(A) Elevated liver enzymes: Isoniazid, rifampin, and pyrazinamide are known to cause hepatotoxicity
While elevated liver enzymes are a serious side effect, they do not typically necessitate the immediate discontinuation of all TB medications, but rather dose adjustment or closer monitoring
(B) Hyperuricemia: Pyrazinamide can cause hyperuricemia
However, hyperuricemia alone usually does not require discontinuation of treatment unless it leads to symptomatic gout
(C) Optic neuritis: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis, which can lead to vision loss
This is a serious side effect and would typically prompt discontinuation of ethambutol to prevent permanent damage
(D) Peripheral neuropathy: Isoniazid can cause peripheral neuropathy
This side effect can often be managed with pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) supplementation rather than discontinuing treatment
(E) Red body excretions: Rifampin can cause red-orange discoloration of body fluids like urine, sweat, and tears
This is a benign side effect and does not require discontinuation of treatment
Step 4: Determining the Most Likely Indication for Discontinuation
Among the options provided, optic neuritis (C) is the most severe and warrants immediate discontinuation of the offending drug (ethambutol) to prevent permanent vision loss
(C) Optic neuritis
